issues.description: Loop invariant for read_from_fifo_when_ready is unstated and the post-fix structure obscures termination
issues.detail: The function maintains an implicit invariant: 'content holds all bytes written so far; loop exits only on true EOF or process death.' That invariant should be stated in a comment. After the fix the outer while-loop has two break paths and a silent pass, and a reader cannot quickly verify termination without tracing fd state changes.

issues.description: Switch to blocking mode lacks literate comment explaining why the prior non-blocking + check_process_exited path was wrong
issues.detail: The removed branch using check_process_exited represented a real hypothesis (macOS may not signal EOF). The new code asserts POSIX guarantees but does not document why the macOS case is now subsumed, nor cite the precise POSIX clause. A careful reader will wonder whether the old bug returns on platforms where the FIFO is opened with quirks. One paragraph of explanation would settle it.

issues.description: fcntl F_SETFL return value unchecked; failure leaves fd in non-blocking mode and the subsequent read loop spins
issues.detail: If fcntl fails (rare but possible on exotic fds), the flag is not cleared and the following os.read calls remain non-blocking. An empty read then returns immediately, the inner 'if not chunk: break' fires, and the function returns partial content, silently reintroducing the original truncation. Verify the syscall succeeded or wrap in try/except with a defined fallback.

issues.description: BlockingIOError handler is now a bare pass with no comment on why it cannot occur after mode switch
issues.detail: Once blocking mode is set, BlockingIOError should not arise from os.read on that fd. The except clause now silently swallows it. State the invariant: 'BlockingIOError only reachable before first data arrives; after that the inner blocking loop owns the fd.' Otherwise the dead-looking branch invites future regressions.

issues.description: Complexity and buffer-size constants (8192) are unjustified and unmeasured
issues.detail: Read chunk size is 8192 bytes; for an 86KB payload that is ~11 syscalls, fine. But the choice deserves one line of comment ('matches typical pipe buffer; larger gives no benefit because PIPE_BUF dominates') so a future reader does not 'optimize' it without measuring. Premature optimization risk is low here, but the constant is load-bearing and undocumented.

issues.description: No test exercises the race; correctness rests on POSIX reasoning alone
issues.detail: Beware of bugs in the above code; I have only proved it correct, not tried it. The PR cites POSIX guarantees but adds no regression test (e.g., a fixture that writes >64KB to a FIFO then exits immediately). A deterministic stress test asserting full payload recovery across N iterations would convert this from UNDER-AUDITED to RIGOROUS.

review.summary: Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED leaning RIGOROUS. The algorithmic claim — that switching to blocking mode after first data yields POSIX-guaranteed complete reads — is sound and the fix is structurally correct. However the code ships without a stated loop invariant, without literate commentary explaining why the prior macOS branch is now unnecessary, without checking fcntl's return, and without a regression test that exercises the original race. The constants and the swallowed BlockingIOError branch also need one-line justifications. Cheap edits would move this from 'probably right' to 'demonstrably right.'
